top_choice_rationale: P002 is a single, sharply defined invention, the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock, with a two-name allocation (Katori for the concept and first realisation, Ye for many-body control at the 10^-18 level) that leaves no forced omission within the supplied names. It has been reproduced and surpassed in independent laboratories and underpins tests of fundamental constants, relativity and geodesy, and a citation scoped to many-atom interrogation distinguishes it from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. P001 is mature and conceptually broader, but the HgTe prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang that directed Molenkamp's experiment stays visibly outside a three-name credit, so I rank it second; an award in either form is better than no award.
